observation_summary: The LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer was failing to use the provided VectorialConvergenceChecker, instead relying solely on internal hardcoded convergence criteria. This led to incorrect optimization results in tests.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves rewriting the convergence logic within the optimization loop. It introduces a new check that prioritizes the user-provided 'checker' if it is not null, and falls back to the internal logic otherwise. This is a procedural change to the optimization algorithm's termination strategy, fitting the Algorithm/Method category.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the addition of 'if (checker != null)' logic to the convergence test block.
The fix_diff_oracle shows the introduction of 'current' and 'previous' state tracking variables to support the convergence checker interface.
The bug report states: 'LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer ignores the VectorialConvergenceChecker parameter passed to it.'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves using an interface (VectorialConvergenceChecker), the root cause is the internal procedural logic of the optimizer failing to invoke that interface, rather than a mismatch in the interface signature itself.
The capability (convergence checking) existed in the design, but the implementation of the optimization loop was missing the logic to correctly utilize it.
